solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: See 22
Search for water – amount round wicket

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: a dose is a measured amount of medicine
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a wicket

explanation.surface: A desert survivor measures out a ration of water around the cricket stumps.
explanation.walkthrough: DOSE wraps around W to make DOWSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dowse is to hunt for underground springs with a forked rod or pendulum.

clue.text: Old agents worked for statesman

indicators.note: worked material has been kneaded and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Retired spies once served a political leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked for' reads as employment; 'worked' is the signal and 'for' just joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gladstone was a Victorian Liberal prime minister, four times in office, the classic example of a British statesman.

clue.text: Andi Peters renovated flat

indicators.note: something renovated is rebuilt and refitted, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A TV presenter has done up his apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: Andi Peters is a British television presenter; 'flat' looks like the home he renovated, but it is the adjective defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something dull, uninspired and lacking any spark or excitement.

clue.text: Established a title that’s raised issues

indicators.note: in a down clue, something raised is lifted upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to set something up is to establish it
taken as written
a name is a title for something

explanation.surface: A newly granted title has caused some controversy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issues' looks like a noun for problems but is the verb: SET A NAME read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to flow out or come forth from a source, as light or a smell does.

clue.text: Lover no longer kissed, did you say? Imagine!

indicators.note: asking what someone said points to the sound of the words rather than their spelling

blocks.note: a former lover is an ex, and a peck is a quick kiss

explanation.surface: Someone is stunned to hear that a partner has stopped kissing them.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants 'Imagine!' as an exclamation of surprise; it is the definition, as in 'I imagine so'.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine or suppose that something is the case, as in 'I expect you're tired'.

clue.text: Try out striker in Old Trafford game?

blocks.note: to try something out is to test it
a match is struck to light it

explanation.surface: A football manager gives a new forward a run-out at Manchester United's ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Trafford is Manchester United's football stadium, but there is also an Old Trafford cricket ground that hosts international five-day games; the striker is a match, not a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: A test match is an international cricket fixture, and Old Trafford regularly stages one, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Home help up country

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
aid is help

explanation.surface: Domestic help is in short supply in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up country' reads as the rural interior; 'up' acts on AID alone.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a nation in South Asia, a straightforward example of the definition.

clue.text: Butter from children’s nurse the best ever?

blocks.note: a nanny looks after children
GOAT is slang for Greatest Of All Time

explanation.surface: Someone praises the butter made by the family nanny as the finest ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is not the spread but one who butts.
explanation.definitionFit: Goats famously charge and head-butt, so a female goat is literally something that butts.

clue.text: Lead removed from gold, say, and the rest

indicators.note: a lead is the front position, so taking it away drops the opening letter

blocks.note: gold is an example of a metal

explanation.surface: Someone strips a lead coating from gold and other materials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' pretends to be the metal Pb; it means the first letter of METAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Et al is the Latin abbreviation for et alii, meaning and others, used at the end of lists.

clue.text: Lawman has whiskey before riotous tea party

indicators.note: a riotous scene is disorderly and wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sheriff knocks back whiskey before a wild tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: The whiskey is just its letter W, and the riotous party is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Wyatt Earp was a famous Wild West marshal, known for the gunfight at the O.K. Corral.

clue.text: Irishman seats Democrat in chair

indicators.note: to seat someone is to place them inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: Sean is a common Irish man's name
D is the standard abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: An Irish host shows an American Democrat to a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In chair' looks like where the Democrat is seated, but 'in' just links and 'chair' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair is an enclosed seat carried on poles by two bearers, once used in cities.

clue.text: Comfort Labour’s leader drawing support

indicators.note: a leader goes at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: ease is comfort
the first letter of the party name

explanation.surface: The Labour leader is comforted by gaining public backing.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is a British political party; 'drawing support' reads as winning backing, but 'drawing' only hints at an artist's stand.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that holds up an artist's canvas while painting, so it is a kind of support.

clue.text: Go with a b-business?

blocks.note: taken as written
the stammered first letter of the synonym that follows, so it repeats that word's opening letter
a company is a business

explanation.surface: A nervous speaker stumbles while recommending a firm to partner with.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter on 'b-business' tells you to stutter the synonym too: business is COMPANY, stammered as C-COMPANY.
explanation.definitionFit: To accompany someone is to go along with them as a companion.

clue.text: Model in quiet bar popped the question

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quiet
a rod is a bar of metal or wood
a model poses for an artist

explanation.surface: A fashion model, in a quiet pub, asked for someone's hand in marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' tempts you towards a pub; here it is a metal or wooden stick, and quiet is the musical p.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop the question is the idiom for making an offer of marriage, which is what proposing means.

clue.text: Daily trim? That keeps things tidy

blocks.note: a daily is a newspaper
to clip is to trim

explanation.surface: A daily haircut is recommended for staying neat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily trim' sounds like grooming; 'daily' is a noun here, a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper clip holds loose sheets together, keeping documents neat and organised on a desk.

clue.text: Dutiful man supporting old bishop

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits beneath it, so it is placed second

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
B is the chess notation for bishop
a man can be a manservant

explanation.surface: A loyal servant props up an elderly bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' puts the man under the old bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Observant in its religious sense means strictly keeping rules and duties, so dutiful fits.

clue.text: Right numpties rolling drunk?

indicators.note: something rolling turns over and over, so the letters are turned back to front

blocks.note: OK means right or correct
a numpty is a Scottish word for an idiot, as is a nit

explanation.surface: A proper pair of idiots staggering home after the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling drunk' is a stock phrase, but 'rolling' reverses OK NITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinko is a slang adjective for heavily intoxicated, like plastered or sozzled.

clue.text: Knight airborne, thrown: trivial problem

indicators.note: something thrown is tossed about, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
taken as written

explanation.surface: A knight sent flying from his horse faces an easy situation.
explanation.walkthrough: The knight is the chess N, and 'airborne' supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-brainer is informal for a decision or question so easy it needs no thought.

clue.text: Instrument at home opening red wine

indicators.note: opening something up lets another thing go inside it

blocks.note: claret is a red Bordeaux wine
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A musician at home uncorks a bottle of red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' reads as uncorking a bottle, but it says the home piece goes into the wine. Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a woodwind instrument with a single reed.

clue.text: Delight where properties initially let?

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
to lease a property is to let it out

explanation.surface: A landlord is overjoyed that houses have found tenants straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially let' reads as first rented, but 'initially' acts on properties and 'let' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To delight someone is to make them happy, a strong sense of the verb to please.

clue.text: Some characters move a table round pub

indicators.note: to move things is to shift them about, so the letters are rearranged
to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: taken as written
PH is the map abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: Some locals shift a table around the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The characters are letters, not people; PH is the Ordnance Survey map label for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An alphabet is a set of letters, and letters are written characters.

clue.text: French writer leaving cheese for monstrous female

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: Émile Zola was a French novelist
Gorgonzola is an Italian blue cheese

explanation.surface: A French author walks away from the cheese board in favour of a fearsome woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The cheese ends in the writer's name; removing him leaves the monster.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gorgons of Greek myth, such as Medusa, were female monsters with snakes for hair.

clue.text: Short book is good to adapt, about right for a film

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the final letter is dropped
to adapt something is to alter it into a new form, so the letters are reworked
about means around, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: to book a seat is to reserve it
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A short novel is ripe for adapting into a screenplay, with the rights sorted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' is the verb, reserve, docked of its last letter; the reshuffled IS GOOD goes round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Reservoir Dogs is Quentin Tarantino's 1992 heist movie, his first feature.

clue.text: Covering line written by playwright

blocks.note: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A dramatist writes a line of stage directions about a cover.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, the line is written beneath the playwright, so his name comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A shawl is a piece of fabric worn over the shoulders, a type of wrap.

clue.text: Son caring for insect population

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
warm means kind-hearted and caring

explanation.surface: A boy tends lovingly to his bug collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caring for' reads as looking after; 'for' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a large mass of bees or other insects moving together.

clue.text: Fix some pot-au-feu for instance?

blocks.note: first meaning: a predicament, as in being in a fix
second meaning: a slow-cooked French dish of meat and vegetables

explanation.surface: A cook rustles up a portion of French casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' looks like a verb, to make some food, but it is a noun meaning a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a stew means being in a state of worry or trouble, and pot-au-feu is a classic braised dish.

clue.text: Temperature in Rome disrupted rail system

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another
something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A heatwave in Rome has caused chaos on the city's trains.
explanation.walkthrough: Rome is not the setting but the letters to rearrange, with T placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A metro is an underground or urban railway network, like the Paris or Rome systems.

clue.text: High city wall has anaemic guards

indicators.note: to guard something is to keep it within, so the letters sit inside the phrase

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A town's ramparts are protected by pale, sickly sentries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guards' looks like a noun for sentries; it is the verb holding the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa, capital of Tibet, sits about 3,650 metres up, one of the world's highest cities.

clue.text: Biscuit and drink with German fan

blocks.note: gin is a drink
Ger is the abbreviation for German
a nut is an enthusiast, as in a fitness nut

explanation.surface: A German enthusiast enjoys a biscuit with a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The fan is an enthusiast, not a cooling device. A ginger nut is a hard British ginger biscuit, like a gingersnap.
explanation.definitionFit: A ginger nut is a crisp, spicy cookie, a familiar type of British biscuit for dunking in tea.

clue.text: Historical region spread to preserve a language

indicators.note: to preserve something is to keep it safe inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: pâté is a savoury spread
taken as written
Latin is a language

explanation.surface: A historic area extends its reach to keep a local tongue alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a verb about territory expanding; it is the noun pâté.
explanation.definitionFit: The Palatinate was a territory of the Holy Roman Empire in western Germany, ruled by a count palatine.

clue.text: Carbon-free load in mythical ship

indicators.note: to be free of something is to be without it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
cargo is a ship's load

explanation.surface: A legendary vessel carries an environmentally clean cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carbon-free' reads as green; it says remove C from the load.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the vessel of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek legend, sailing for the Golden Fleece.
